capabilities.title: The window is gone
capabilities.requirement: no crate depends on the window toolkit; the tree holds no webview interface, no IPC router and no gate that boots a window, audits one or samples its frames; the tests that drive them leave with them and the remaining gate is green; the masters say in plain words that this version has no interface and which later version brings a minimal one on another toolkit; the 0.3.0 capabilities that were about the window are recorded as retired with the surface, not as regressed
capabilities.observed_gap: a Tauri shell and a webview interface (`pulse-app/ui`, 243 tracked files), ten IPC router files (`pulse-app/src/*_router.rs`), the tray, the window and its geometry, the updater and the notification plugin; the gates that exist for it (`a11y` and `boot` CI jobs, the webview suite, and in `xtask` the webview drive, staged gate, smoke, npm gate, hue shift, discovery, self-verify, frame sampling and bundle format); three masters whose subject it is (design-system, layout-templates, a11y-plan). Most of 0.3.0's 22 verified capabilities are about it; the route names which, id by id.

verification.acceptance: No crate's dependency graph holds the window toolkit; the tree holds no webview interface, no IPC router and no gate that boots, audits or frame-samples a window; the engine's own gate is green without them and everything it detected before is still detected; the three interface masters state that this version has no interface and which later version brings one; each 0.3.0 capability that was about the window reads retired with the surface in the capability record.

capabilities.title: The local model is gone from the engine, with everything that served it
capabilities.requirement: the engine starts, detects and reports with no model present and none configured; no gate needs a GPU; no crate, example, script, environment variable, vendored runtime or experiment that exists for a local model remains, and their tests leave with them; the experiments directory is gone from the dev host, shown by a listing because no commit can show it; the words of a report come from the engine's own facts (P-099); a large model reads through the door (P-092) and is not part of the engine
capabilities.observed_gap: `crates/interpretation` (10 tracked files, about 3700 lines: runner trait, prompt builders, the `L4Output` schema, degraded mode); in `pulse-app` the inference runtimes, the model router, the hardware profile, the grammar file; the decision probe (three files under `pulse-app/examples/`, about 10,500 lines) and the latency grader; six `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` environment variables for the model, one of which `xtask` still sets; `experiments/` (git-ignored, no tracked file: a directory on the dev host) and a vendored `llama-cpp`.

verification.acceptance: On a host with no model and no GPU, and none configured, the engine starts, detects a planted fault and reports it in words drawn from its own facts; no gate needs a GPU; the tree holds no crate, example, script, environment variable, vendored runtime or experiment that exists for a local model, and their tests are gone with them; a listing shows the experiments directory gone from the dev host.

capabilities.title: The corpus is stored unencrypted, for this first stage
capabilities.requirement: the engine keeps its stores readable on its own node with no credential store, and no code or dependency for one remains; the secret scrubber at ingest stays as it is; the security master records the decision, its date and that it is to be looked at again
capabilities.observed_gap: the incident corpus is encrypted per cell with a key from the desktop's credential store (`crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs`, `encryption.rs`; the `keyring` and `aes-gcm` dependencies); a server has no such store (a CI runner already read `KeyringUnavailable`); the buffer is not encrypted.

verification.acceptance: On a node with no credential store the engine opens, writes and reads back its stores across a restart; the dependency graph and the tree hold no code for a credential store or for encrypting the corpus; a secret planted in telemetry is still scrubbed before anything is stored; the security master records the decision, its date and that it is to be looked at again.

capabilities.title: A program without a window
capabilities.requirement: the engine is a console program that runs in the background on a Linux server and is driven by commands; nothing in it needs a display, a GPU or a desktop session; everything 0.3.0 detected is still detected
capabilities.observed_gap: one application binary that is a Tauri process; no headless mode.

verification.acceptance: The engine starts as a console program on a Linux server with no display, no GPU and no desktop session, runs in the background and answers its commands; every kind of finding 0.3.0 detected, one incident for a sustained storm and automatic resolution are each still observed on the same telemetry.

capabilities.title: Telemetry arrives over a network
capabilities.requirement: a service on another host sends OTLP to the engine with a token over an encrypted channel; a request without the token is refused; connecting a service takes an address and a token and installs nothing beside it
capabilities.observed_gap: the receivers bind `127.0.0.1`, the HTTP one admits only localhost `Host` values (`crates/ingest/src/http.rs:113-117`), and neither asks for a credential.

verification.acceptance: A service on another host, given only an address and a token and with nothing installed beside it, sends OTLP to the engine over an encrypted channel and its telemetry is received; the same request without the token is refused.

capabilities.title: What the network receiver refuses
capabilities.requirement: a request with a missing or wrong token is refused before its body is read, and the refusal is recorded without the token's value; the token is made, shown once, replaced and revoked by an engine command and is never written to a log or a report; it is stated who terminates the encrypted channel and where its private key lives — never in a store the door reads, never in a log; a sender that exceeds its rate is slowed or refused without starving another; the existing size and count invariants apply to a remote sender; a plain unencrypted connection from another host is refused; everything the scrubber removes today is still removed before anything is stored
capabilities.observed_gap: the receiver's only guards today are its localhost bind, a `Host` allow-list, size and count invariants and a global rate limit; none of them assumes a sender it does not trust.

verification.acceptance: A request with a missing or wrong token is refused before its body is read and the refusal is recorded without the token's value; the token is made, shown once, replaced and revoked by an engine command and appears in no log and no report; who terminates the encrypted channel and where its private key lives are stated, and the key lies in no store the door reads and in no log; a sender over its rate is slowed or refused while another sender is still served; a request beyond the size or count limits is rejected from a remote sender as from a local one; a plain unencrypted connection from another host is refused; a secret in accepted telemetry is scrubbed before storage.

capabilities.title: The watcher counts by event time
capabilities.requirement: every check reasons by the time stamped inside the record, with a stated allowance for lateness; a batch that arrives late is counted where it belongs, and a recorded stream can be played again and give the same result; a record stamped in the future beyond a stated allowance cannot move what the checks take for the present, and what is done with such a record is stated
capabilities.observed_gap: windows, the restart detector and the retention cutoff read the system clock; the restart cue keys on a gap in ARRIVAL of more than 20 s.

verification.acceptance: Each check gives the same answer for a stream however its batches arrive within the stated lateness allowance: a late batch is counted in the window its stamps belong to; a recorded stream played twice yields identical findings; a record stamped in the future beyond the stated allowance does not move what the checks take for the present, and what is done with such a record is stated and observed.

capabilities.title: The node is small
capabilities.requirement: the engine fits a 1 GB node under a long run; the figure is measured, and the database file does not grow without bound under constant insert and delete; the engine's own log is bounded in total size, so neither can fill the node
capabilities.observed_gap: the engine's memory use with a database on disk has never been measured. The engine's log rotates daily (`pulse-app/src/observability.rs:2645`) and nothing removes an old file.

verification.acceptance: Under a long run on a node with 1 GB of memory the engine's measured memory stays inside the node and the figure is recorded; under constant insert and delete the database file stops growing; the engine's own log stays under a stated total size however long the engine runs, so neither can fill the node.

capabilities.title: What was received is still there tomorrow
capabilities.requirement: raw telemetry is kept 7 days by default, the term configurable, with a ceiling on the store's size beside it at which the oldest goes first, and survives a restart; what the watcher has learned survives a restart; a gap while the engine was down is not read as the service's silence; whether a week fits the node's disk under a real stream is measured, and the ceiling's figure is set from that reading
capabilities.observed_gap: raw telemetry lives 600 s in an in-memory database; only incidents persist; the learned baseline is discarded at start when older than an hour.

verification.acceptance: Telemetry received is still readable the next day and after a restart; with default settings it is kept 7 days, the term can be changed, and at the store's size ceiling the oldest goes first; what the watcher had learned before a restart is in use after it; time the engine was down is not reported as the service's silence; a week of a real stream on the node's disk is measured and the ceiling's figure is set from that reading.

capabilities.title: The agent's door opens onto the real data, from the engine's first step
capabilities.requirement: the door lives inside the engine's process and replaces the stdio sidecar as soon as the console engine exists, ahead of the removals the sidecar is built on (the credential store, the resolver, the incident it parses, the model's renderer, the workspace key), so that those chunks change the door, which stays, and never the sidecar, which goes; every reading from outside the process — the engine's own end-to-end gate, the external harness at each theme — goes through the door; an agent on the developer's machine reaches the engine's tools and reads the telemetry the engine holds, filtered by service, time range, trace and text, with aggregates; it reaches one incident whole, with its evidence, and the incidents like it from the past; it can ask for the curated snapshot — a narrow, budgeted view of recent telemetry made for a large model — which is that code's consumer from now on; the same door serves the test harness and the status widget
capabilities.observed_gap: the MCP sidecar's four telemetry tools read their own empty in-memory database and accept only a time window and a limit; the curated snapshot and the curation crates (about 3200 lines) have the window's toast and that empty database as their only outlets. The sidecar is a second process built on what this version removes: it opens the corpus through the desktop's credential store (`crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:6`), reads the published workspace key (`:78`), and renders an incident by parsing the model's answer with the model's renderer (`crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:25-28`, `:380`). Until a door exists it is the only way anything outside the process reads a finding.

verification.acceptance: From the first step in which a console engine exists, every reading from outside its process goes through a door inside that process: the engine's own end-to-end gate and the external harness at each theme read through it, no stdio sidecar exists, and no later removal has a sidecar to change; an agent on the developer's machine reads through it the telemetry the engine holds, filtered by service, time range, trace and text, with aggregates, one incident whole with its evidence and the incidents like it from the past, and the curated snapshot of recent telemetry; the test harness and the status command use the same door.

capabilities.title: What the door may do
capabilities.requirement: until the engine accepts connections from another host, the door answers on the engine's own host only; from the moment it can be reached from another host it answers only a party the node's owner has admitted, and admission has a lifecycle: how a party is admitted and how it is revoked, as the token has; it is stated where an admitted party's credential lives on the developer's machine — never in a repository, never in a log; the door is encrypted in transit; it reads the engine's stores (telemetry, incidents, reports, the engine's own state) and nothing else on the node: not the token, not configuration secrets, not files outside those stores; every answer is bounded in size and time, so no question can exhaust the node; what it returns was scrubbed at ingest; the one write it keeps (resolving an incident) is named as a write and can be switched off
capabilities.observed_gap: the sidecar's tools are local, unauthenticated, and one of them writes (it marks an incident resolved).

verification.acceptance: Before the engine accepts connections from another host the door answers on the engine's own host only; once it can be reached from another host it answers only an admitted party, a party is admitted and revoked in a stated way and a revoked party is refused; where an admitted party's credential lives on the developer's machine is stated, outside any repository and any log; the door's traffic is encrypted in transit; a request for the token, a configuration secret or a file outside the stores is refused; an answer too large or too slow is cut at a stated bound; what it returns was scrubbed at ingest; resolving an incident is named as a write and can be switched off.

capabilities.title: A span keeps its meaning
capabilities.requirement: the stored span keeps its name, kind and parent, the service's version and environment, and the attributes that say which route, which status code, which database or peer it touched, under both generations of the semantic-convention names; who calls whom can be answered from what is stored
capabilities.observed_gap: a span is stored as seven fields; its name, kind, parent, status message, every attribute and every resource attribute but `service.name` are dropped at ingest.

verification.acceptance: A stored span, read back, carries its name, kind and parent, the service's version and environment, and the attributes naming the route, the status code, the database or the peer, whichever generation of the semantic-convention names the sender used; for a stream with known callers the question who calls whom is answered correctly from what is stored.

capabilities.title: Metrics and logs keep theirs
capabilities.requirement: a percentile can be computed from stored metrics; a log line and a metric point name their service; exception type, message and stack are readable through the door
capabilities.observed_gap: histogram-family points are stored as the value 0; a log row and a metric row carry no service identity; stored exception text has no reader.

verification.acceptance: A percentile computed from stored metrics matches the distribution that was sent; every stored log line and metric point names its service; an exception's type, message and stack are read back through the door.

capabilities.title: A new kind of error is news
capabilities.requirement: the first appearance of an error for a service is a finding, in whichever of the three encodings it arrives (a span's error status, an exception on a span, a high-severity log), and so is the return of one that had gone away
capabilities.observed_gap: the fingerprint feeds the retry-storm detector and the search for similar past incidents; nothing says "this error was never seen before". An error reaches the engine in three encodings — a span's error status, an exception on a span, a high-severity log — and only the second is fingerprinted.

verification.acceptance: The first time an error appears for a service a finding is raised, whether it arrives as a span's error status, an exception on a span or a high-severity log; a repeat of a known error raises none; an error that had gone away and returns raises one.

capabilities.title: A release is compared with the one before
capabilities.requirement: when a new version of a service appears, the engine compares it with the previous one (error rate, new error kinds, latency, per operation where the operation is known) and says when the new one is worse, naming the version and the moment it appeared
capabilities.observed_gap: the service version is dropped at ingest; nothing knows a release happened.

verification.acceptance: When a new version of a service appears the engine records the version and the moment it appeared, compares it with the previous one on error rate, new error kinds and latency, per operation where the operation is known, and says so when the new one is worse; a release that is no worse raises nothing.

capabilities.title: Silence is told apart from "nothing arrived"
capabilities.requirement: "the service went quiet", "no data reached the engine" and "the check could not be evaluated" are three different states, and a recovery is announced
capabilities.observed_gap: a vanished stream and an engine that could not receive look alike.

verification.acceptance: A service that stops sending, an engine that no data reached and a check that could not be evaluated are reported as three different states, and the recovery from each is announced.

capabilities.title: The engine says it, in one line and in a report
capabilities.requirement: a command of the engine prints the current state in one line a desktop panel can show; a change of state raises a system notification; the notification carries a short report (what, where, since when, after which version, which errors are new) written without a model; this is the one report form (P-112)
capabilities.observed_gap: findings are visible only inside the window.

verification.acceptance: A command of the engine prints the current state in one line and a panel on the founder's desktop shows it; a change of state raises a system notification carrying a short report that says what, where, since when, after which version and which errors are new, written with no model in its path; no second report form exists.

capabilities.title: The report is enough for a large model
capabilities.requirement: given the report and the door, a large model names the cause that was planted; the report is narrow and names its evidence by identifier; "not enough data" is an honest answer the engine can give
capabilities.observed_gap: no measurement exists of whether a large model can work from a report of the engine's.

verification.acceptance: Given only the engine's report and the door, a large model names the planted cause, measured over a set of planted faults; the report is narrow and names its evidence by identifier; where the data cannot support a finding the engine answers that there is not enough data.

capabilities.title: A real service is watched too
capabilities.requirement: one real service of the founder's sends its telemetry to the engine for days; what the engine reported and what it stayed silent on is read against what actually happened to that service; he names the service together with the personal data its telemetry carries, and before its first send each kind he names is either scrubbed before storage or its keeping is decided and recorded; until then the security master's "Compliance triggers: None" keeps its present basis
capabilities.observed_gap: every reading of Pulse so far was taken on telemetry a test tool composed.

verification.acceptance: The founder names one real service and the personal data its telemetry carries; before its first send each named kind is either scrubbed before storage or its keeping is decided and recorded; the service then sends for days, and what the engine reported and what it stayed silent on is read against what actually happened to it; until the naming, the security master's statement that there are no compliance triggers stands on its present basis.

capabilities.title: The bad-version scenario, end to end (dynamic-external)
capabilities.requirement: Conductor rolls out a "bad version" of one service in its simulated world, over the network, to an engine on another host; within minutes the panel module and a system notification carry a message naming the service, the version and the new error; a large model, given the report and the door, names the planted cause; the engine did this on a 1 GB node and stayed silent through the healthy hours before it

verification.acceptance: Conductor rolls out a bad version of one service in its simulated world, over the network, to an engine on another host with 1 GB of memory; within minutes the panel line and a system notification name the service, the version and the new error; a large model given the report and the door names the planted cause; through the healthy hours before the rollout the engine raised nothing; after each theme the harness's reading of that theme, taken through the door from input to output, is recorded.

capabilities.title: The check before a push runs on Linux
capabilities.requirement: the check a developer runs before a push runs natively on the Linux dev host over the stages that survive this version's removals
capabilities.observed_gap: `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` needs `wsl.exe`; on the Linux dev host its stages are run by hand.

verification.acceptance: On the Linux dev host one check runs natively before a push, over every stage that survives this version's removals, with no second operating system involved, and gives a verdict.

capabilities.title: The plugin host is gone
capabilities.requirement: the workspace depends on no WebAssembly runtime; no plugin host or example is in the tree; the critical path that drove the plugin lifecycle is recorded as retired, not regressed
capabilities.observed_gap: `crates/plugins`, the `wasmtime` dependency, `plugins-examples/`, and the critical path that drives the plugin lifecycle.

verification.acceptance: The workspace's dependency graph holds no WebAssembly runtime; the tree holds no plugin host and no example plugin; the capability record reads the plugin-lifecycle critical path as retired with the surface, not regressed; the engine's gate is green without it.

capabilities.title: Workspace detection is gone
capabilities.requirement: the engine reads no project folder; one engine watches one product: its incidents live in its one store and are told apart by the check and the service alone; nothing takes the workspace key's place, and in this version a sender's token is not an incident key — the same storm sent under two tokens forms one incident; incidents are formed, kept, listed and resolved the same from wherever the engine is started
capabilities.observed_gap: `crates/workspace-detector` reads the directory the application was started in; incidents are keyed by the workspace it detects (the registry's cooldown key, `incidents.workspace` and three `WHERE workspace` queries, a key file published for the sidecar).

verification.acceptance: The engine reads no project folder; started from two different directories against the same stores it forms, keeps, lists and resolves the same incidents; storms that differ by check or by service form separate incidents, and the same storm sent under two tokens forms one; nothing stands where the workspace key stood.

capabilities.title: The training export is gone
capabilities.requirement: no export exists and nothing the engine writes lands outside its own stores
capabilities.observed_gap: `pulse-app/src/training_export.rs` and its route write incidents to the user's Downloads folder for model training.

verification.acceptance: No export of incidents exists among the engine's commands or the door's answers; after a full run every file the engine wrote lies inside its own stores.

capabilities.title: The engine reaches a node
capabilities.requirement: the engine is delivered as one Linux binary with a documented way to run it as a service; on a clean node the documented steps give an engine that runs, comes back after a restart and receives telemetry; the binary comes with a checksum, and the documented steps verify it
capabilities.observed_gap: the only delivery is the desktop bundle R8 removes, and its signing goes with it.

verification.acceptance: On a clean Linux node the documented steps verify the binary's checksum, put the one binary in place and run it as a service; the engine runs, comes back after the node restarts and receives telemetry.

capabilities.title: The bridge leaves the engine's crates
capabilities.requirement: no engine crate carries a feature, a derive or a dependency that exists for an IPC bridge; the engine's configuration is the engine's own and holds no key about an interface; the bridge crate is gone
capabilities.observed_gap: `tauri` itself is declared only by `pulse-app` and optionally by `crates/ui-bridge` (5 files, about 4800 lines), but the bridge's types reach into the engine: the ingest and triage crates carry a default-on `taurpc-runtime` feature with `specta` derives, `crates/viz` depends on `specta` unconditionally, and the engine's own configuration schema (`Settings`) lives in the bridge crate, read by `crates/config-watcher`, with keys for a theme, a widget position, always-on-top and a snapshot preset. R1's first clause would be met without touching any of this.

verification.acceptance: No engine crate carries a feature, a type derive or a dependency that exists for an IPC bridge, and the bridge crate is absent; the engine reads its configuration from its own definition, which holds no key about an interface, and a configuration change still takes effect while the engine runs.

capabilities.title: What was computed only to be shown is gone
capabilities.requirement: the engine does no work whose only reader was the window: no stream topic, no per-batch encode for a subscriber that does not exist, no display state; the service registry's liveness truth stays engine state
capabilities.observed_gap: the buffer encodes every batch to Arrow IPC and broadcasts it on thirteen `pulse://stream/*` topics whose only production subscriber is the window's channel (`pulse-app/src/streams.rs:36-48`); triage computes state for display alone — the effective tier for the halo (`crates/triage/src/incident/tier_effective.rs`), the constellation metrics, the discovery observer.

verification.acceptance: With telemetry flowing, the engine publishes no stream topic, encodes no batch for a subscriber that does not exist and computes no display state; the service registry still tells a live service from one that went quiet, and detection is unchanged.

capabilities.title: The digest is gone
capabilities.requirement: the engine builds with no network access and no tokenizer; it assembles no prompt, counts no tokens and archives no digest; the digest archive table is gone; the search for similar past incidents is kept and lives where incidents live; the half-hour rate defect is closed by the code's removal, not carried
capabilities.observed_gap: `crates/triage/src/digest/` (6 files, about 2800 lines) assembles a token-budgeted text — budgets of 500, 2000 and 3000 tokens, an embedded Llama-3 tokenizer, a last-write-wins queue, a damper against standing GPU load — and broadcasts it. Its subscribers are the model and a persister that writes every digest to the corpus table `digest_archive`, which nothing reads. The triage crate downloads that tokenizer from a third-party host at first build (`crates/triage/build.rs`). The recorded defect "the half-hour digest's rate is divided by a literal 60" (`.andromeda/residuals.md:27`) lives in this code.

verification.acceptance: The engine builds with no network access and no tokenizer; while running it assembles no prompt, counts no tokens and archives no digest, and its incident store holds no digest archive; an incident still comes with the incidents like it from the past, found where incidents live; the half-hour rate defect cannot occur because the code that computed it is gone.

capabilities.title: The cadence coordinator is gone
capabilities.requirement: nothing in the engine decides when a model should run; no hardware profile, tier or reflection cadence remains, no configuration key for one, and no handle to one in the cue emitter
capabilities.observed_gap: `crates/triage/src/cadence/` (4 files, about 1600 lines) has four modes — three tiers and a 1800 s "reflection" — and a gate on a GPU/CPU hardware profile. A cycle runs seven aggregation queries, keeps only whether each succeeded (`coordinator.rs:190`), and sends a trigger for the digest. None of it serves detection, but the cue emitter is handed its trigger channel (`crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs:399-402`).

verification.acceptance: Nothing in the running engine decides when a model should run: no hardware profile, tier or reflection cadence exists, no configuration key names one and the cue emitter holds no handle to one; every check still fires on its own evidence as before.

capabilities.title: An incident is the engine's own record
capabilities.requirement: an incident stores what the engine knows (which check found it, in which service, since when, after which version, which errors, which evidence by identifier) and nothing shaped as a model's answer; one report form exists, the one P-099 describes, and the old renderer is gone; a store written by 0.3.0 is not read: the engine on a node starts from its own empty stores
capabilities.observed_gap: an incident's content is a field holding the model's `L4Output` as JSON (`crates/triage/src/contract.rs:462`); its title and detail are the model's; the report an agent retrieves renders the model's sections — hypotheses, investigation steps, project context, a resolution summary — and a `degraded_mode` flag that would read true for every incident once no model runs (`crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs`, `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:366-392`).

verification.acceptance: A newly formed incident, read back, states which check found it, in which service, since when, after which version, with which errors and which evidence by identifier, and carries nothing shaped as a model's answer; exactly one report form exists and the old renderer is gone; an engine started beside a store written by 0.3.0 does not read it and starts from its own empty stores.

capabilities.title: The other operating systems are gone from the code
capabilities.requirement: the tree builds, tests and runs on Linux alone and holds no branch, script, link hint or workaround for another operating system; CI has no leg for one
capabilities.observed_gap: seven `.ps1` files (754 lines); the `wsl.exe` hop in `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`; five `pwsh`/`powershell` spawns in `xtask`; Windows path handling (`\\?\`) in `crates/config-watcher`; `rstrtmgr` link hints in three build scripts; an MSVC linker override in `.cargo/config.toml`; `[lib] test = false` in `pulse-app/Cargo.toml`, a WebView2 workaround; data-directory names for Windows and macOS in five source files; Windows and macOS legs in three CI jobs.

verification.acceptance: The tree builds, tests and runs on Linux alone; it holds no branch, script, link hint or workaround for another operating system; every CI job runs on Linux only and is green.

capabilities.title: The desktop's distribution is gone
capabilities.requirement: no workflow, runbook, test or bot configuration for a desktop bundle, an updater, a package channel or an npm tree remains; the two external channel repositories, `turbolet85/homebrew-andromeda-pulse` and `turbolet85/scoop-andromeda-pulse`, are the founder's to retire by hand and are named on the card
capabilities.observed_gap: `release.yml` builds desktop bundles for three systems; `update-channels.yml` (411 lines) publishes to a Homebrew tap and a Scoop bucket; two runbooks describe the release environment and the updater's key rotation; a test pins the channel manifests; the dependency bot watches an npm tree.

verification.acceptance: The tree holds no workflow, runbook, test or bot configuration for a desktop bundle, an updater, a package channel or an npm tree; the removing chunk's card names the two external channel repositories for the founder to retire by hand; the engine's own gate is green without them.

capabilities.title: The log allowlist describes this engine
capabilities.requirement: every allowed log target is one the engine can emit; none names a window, a model, a digest, a tray or a plugin
capabilities.observed_gap: `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` allows 215 log targets by name; by their names at least 35 are the window's and 42 the model's or the digest's; eighteen tests pin them.

verification.acceptance: Every log target the allowlist admits is one the running engine emits, and none names a window, a model, a digest, a tray or a plugin.

capabilities.title: The records say what the product is
capabilities.requirement: every record a newcomer or an agent reads first describes a console engine on its own node, for one developer with one product; no rule instructs what this version removes or forbids what it adds; what describes 0.2–0.3 is either gone or marked as the history of those versions; the security master's tier, auth model and attack surface are restated for a networked engine with stores on disk, no later than the chunk that opens the network receiver, and what follows is built to the restated tier
capabilities.observed_gap: `.andromeda/input.md`, `andromeda-pulse-product-description.md`, `.andromeda/project.yaml` and architecture §Project Intent call the product a cross-platform desktop dashboard — "Not a web app, not a CLI"; `CLAUDE.md` opens "Cross-platform Tauri 2 desktop dashboard"; three `.claude/rules` files are scoped to the webview; the security rule an agent always loads says the receivers "MUST bind to 127.0.0.1 only … no auth model", which contradicts F2; `docs/v0_2_0/` (seven files, about 5200 lines) describes the local-model product as current.
